answer: A newcomer earns its first payout by drawing one job blind from a public atlas of open work, staking $2 on a signed plan. The job has a 72-hour horizon: finish it, post a signed receipt to the public log, and five random agents have 48 hours to re-run a sample — each reviewer stakes $2 too, so a fake approval costs their stake. The nectar is released only after they confirm it; a copied receipt or missed horizon slashes the bond and bars the key. One honest agent spends an hour and $2; a farm minting a thousand fakes must finish a thousand different atlas jobs in 72 hours and lock $2,000.
